name: France by Night: The Hegemony and the Fiefs of the Camarilla

text.content:
French Kindred society is unusually traditionalist even by European standards: centuries of revolutions, invasions, and religious wars taught the Elders a near-paranoid respect for the Six Traditions, above all the Masquerade, which is better kept in France than almost anywhere else in the world. Most French Kindred feed by the so-called "Casanova method" — cultivating small, closed circles of mortal prey (the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} of Paris favor the capital's fashionable and artistic set) rather than hunting openly in the streets, and those who do hunt the streets (many @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel} and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu}) target the marginalized and the homeless, who are least likely to draw attention.

Rather than the American notion of a "city," French Kindred organize themselves around the Fief, a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue}-originated term for a domain built around one or more urban centers. Since Kindred population density in France runs far higher, proportionally, than the American "one vampire per hundred thousand mortals" rule of thumb (Paris alone housed far more Kindred than that ratio would predict even at the height of the Revolution), Fiefs typically encompass an entire region rather than a single city.

Since the late 16th century, the Prince of Paris has held a unique supreme authority called the Hegemony, functioning as the Kindred equivalent of Absolute Monarchy: every other Prince in France was stripped of the title of Prince (reserved solely for whoever sits in Paris) and reduced to Marquis, a vassal ruler who answers directly to Paris. Historically the title of Prince persisted among the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} rulers of the south of France until they were overthrown during the Revolution; when the Restoration allowed the Parisian Toreador to reclaim power, they extended the Hegemony over every French Fief. This is why the French @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} never recovered the power they held in the Middle Ages, and pale by comparison to their English and German cousins.

Within their own Fiefs, Marquis hold all the same powers and privileges as a Prince, with two critical exceptions: a Marquis is not elected by the local Primogen but appointed (and revocable at will) by the Prince of Paris, and the Prince holds veto power over every one of a Marquis's decisions, including grants of the right of Embrace. Eight Marquis currently rule France, almost all Ventrue and most descended from the old local princely lines; six major Fiefs (Nord, Est, Normandie, Aquitaine-Occitanie, Marseille, and Lyon) are detailed in this book. In each Fief the Prince also maintains an official representative called a Legate, invariably a Toreador Ancilla answerable only to the Prince and exempt from the local Marquis's authority.

Opposition to the absolute Toreador Hegemony comes less from the Anarchs than from the Praxist movement (from "Praxis," a Prince's right to rule their city): a coalition, originally of bitter conservative old Ventrue, that seeks to restore the title and full sovereign powers of Prince to every Marquis. Several sitting Marquis, starting with the Marquis of Lyon, are open Praxist sympathizers, and the movement has begun favoring the rise of the French far right as a way to build an independent power base free of Kindred influence.

pages.name: Fief Offices and the Six Traditions in France

text.content:
Beyond the Marquis, the Legate, and the Primogen, three offices carry real political weight in a French Fief: the Seneschal (or Regent), the Marquis's first counselor and designated replacement when the Marquis is away or answering a summons to Paris, almost always a direct descendant of the Marquis; the Provost, roughly equivalent to an American Sheriff, who investigates Masquerade breaches and organizes Blood Hunts and may interrogate any Kindred of the Fief, answering only to the Marquis or Seneschal; and the Keeper of Elysium, who is invariably @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} (the Prince automatically vetoes any other candidate) and who greets visiting Kindred at a designated public site called the Atrium (often a nightclub), as required by the Tradition of Hospitality.

The Traditions are interpreted with particular rigor in France. The Masquerade is enforced so severely that repeat or serious offenders are typically exiled outright, encouraged to relocate to more tolerant territories — the United States chief among them. Domain remains a living Tradition rather than a formality: in Paris the largest domains can cover an entire arrondissement, and in the provinces an entire minor city, though this remains a rare privilege reserved for the Primogen and other dignitaries. The right of Embrace is granted with extreme parsimony, almost always as a reward for exceptional service to a Prince or Marquis. Destruction (Blood Hunts) in the provinces are always personally supervised by the Provost; in Paris itself, Blood Hunts are typically delegated to powerful ghouls in the Prince's service known as Lictors, whose jurisdiction can extend across the whole of France — a frequent source of friction with provincial Marquis and Provosts.

pages.name: Clans, Anarchs, and the Sabbat in France

text.content:
The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} are the undisputed masters of Paris, controlling more than two-thirds of the city's recognized Kindred population since the Renaissance; outside the capital their influence is strongest in Toulouse and Avignon. The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} split between the conservative, lineage-obsessed Nobles (five surviving Great Families: De Sens of Paris, De Morsac of Occitania, De Gueldre of the Nord, D'Harcourt of Normandy, and De Vandreuil of Lyon) and the Liberals, secret architects of the Industrial Revolution and today of European unification, centered on Strasbourg. The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} remain divided between anti-@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} Iconoclasts and Idealists who see the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere}, not the Toreador, as the Clan's true enemies. The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} are comparatively weak in France, tied to secret societies rather than open political power, and have never been fully accepted by French Kindred society. The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel} are dwindling, with the last significant French territory in the Basque Country; a handful who remain in Paris display a degenerative condition called the Mal de la Rue ("Street Sickness"), attributed to feeding too heavily on blood tainted by alcohol and drugs. @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.SNuXttNqxzJ6uPXv]{Caitiff} face outright ostracism from @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} society and mostly either join the most violent Anarch factions or emigrate to the more tolerant United States. Nine Tremere Chantries operate in France, coordinated from Orléans by the Tremere Lord of France, who nominally answers to the Prince of Paris.

French Anarchs split between well-tolerated "salon" intellectuals whom Prince Villon regards with amused indulgence, and a more violent Iconoclast fringe tied to far-left terrorist groups, which posed a real threat to the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} in the late 1970s and early 1980s before being ruthlessly hunted down by the Prince's agents.

The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} is far weaker in Europe than in America and controls no French Fief outright, but persistent rumors describe @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} lairs in the Parisian sewers (allegedly protected by Antitribu @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} spies among the loyalist @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu}), a roving Pack of a dozen Sabbat vampires led by a centuries-old @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} and backed by biker gangs, and a "Secret Sabbat" of @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} Elders who infiltrated the Camarilla itself during periods of upheaval (the Revolution, the Occupation), using Vicissitude to assume their victims' identities in order to destabilize the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah}, Toreador, and Ventrue Clans from within.

The Fief du Nord spans the Lille-Roubaix-Tourcoing conurbation out to the Channel ports of Calais and Dunkirk. Once a stronghold of conservative industrialist @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue}, it passed after the Second World War into the hands of Étienne, a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} Marquis — one of the rare @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} Fiefs actually ruled by that Clan. An idealist revolutionary turned reluctant ruler, Étienne is deeply unpopular even among his own Clan, who accuse him of selling out to the Parisian @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador}; he prefers the title Tribune to Marquis and has held power for half a century thanks to distant Princely support and his enemies' inability to unite against him.

Reynier, Embraced during the Revolution by Marguerite Foccart, leads the Idealist opposition within the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} Clan and is widely seen as Étienne's most likely successor, though he would back the Marquis in any real crisis rather than see power fall to the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} or @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere}. Ianka, a Polish resistance fighter Embraced in 1942, is the icon of the Anarch movement in the region and Étienne's chief rival within his own Clan, hiding sharp political intelligence behind a deliberately impulsive, violent Iconoclast facade.

The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} Absinthe, Embraced at the end of the last century from one of the Nord's mining-town brothels, haunts Lille's clubs and bars as a seductive, elusive prostitute with no fixed haven. Provost Crevel, who emerged mysteriously during the Occupation and is believed to have engineered Étienne's rise to power, commands the Fief's extensive @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} spy network and is widely regarded as the Fief's true second power — a role he does not let Étienne forget.

The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} Legate Marc-Antoine, of the Prince's own line, rarely intervenes in local affairs, preferring Parisian company; Alexia, Embraced in the 1920s, is the Fief's Keeper of Elysium and the region's leading Poseur, holding court over a rotating circle of beautiful young admirers at the Atrium nightclub, Les Âmes Mortes. The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} Chantry is riven by a power struggle between Regent Maucroix, an ambitious 18th-century Tremere who rose during the confusion of the Revolution and Empire, and his own descendant Marianne Dupuy, protected from Maucroix's wrath by Justicar Karl Schrekt himself. Deposed Ventrue Marquis Laurent de Gueldre, who lost power in 1945 and still commands considerable regional influence, remains Étienne's most determined enemy, along with his own former protégé Philippe, the young leader of a rising "eurocrat" Ventrue faction who engineered de Gueldre's financial ruin.

Secret: beneath the Nord's ports lies the Labyrinth, an enormous private @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} tunnel network (linking disused mines, abandoned sewers, quarries, and wartime bunkers from Dunkirk to Cherbourg) that is Provost Crevel's personal domain. Recent expansion work has awakened a torpid Nictuku, which now stalks the tunnels and has already claimed several Nosferatu; Crevel, unable to identify the threat, has simply sealed off the affected sections rather than admit his ignorance.

The Fief of Normandy unites Rouen (the capital), Le Havre (a major industrial port), and Caen (a sleepy bourgeois city). Once powerful, it has become a mere province of Paris in all but name. Its nominal ruler, the ancient @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} Marquis D'Harcourt, is a broken figure: after centuries in torpor imposed as punishment for plotting against Prince Beatrix during the Fronde, he was restored to his title in the 1820s but emerged half-mad, unable to adapt to the modern world, and prone to frenzies triggered by the sight of modern technology. He periodically withdraws to the Channel Island of Sercq, whose medieval pace of life soothes him, while continuing a private war against the English branch of Clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} out of loyalty to his sire's ally, the Methuselah Mithras.

Real power belongs to Regent Quentin, Embraced at the end of the 16th century and Blood Bound since childehood to @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} Prince François Villon, whom he serves as a loyal spymaster; Quentin lets D'Harcourt rage against the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} undisturbed while quietly running the Fief for Paris. Helen Drake, a determined London-born businesswoman, leads the English @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} faction that manipulates D'Harcourt and worries both Quentin and, reportedly, Villon himself.

Vincent, the oldest known @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} of the Fief (Embraced at the turn of the century, a former literature professor and Marxist activist), leads Le Havre's Anarchs and dreams of turning the port into an independent "Free City." The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} Ancilla Euphrasie, Embraced after being committed to Caen's psychiatric hospital as a teenager for denouncing the priest who abused her, rules that asylum still, occasionally intervening to protect innocent mortals despite her madness. The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} Antifer commands the Fief's port-side information network like a spider at the center of its web, and is suspected by the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} of eliminating several of their own who strayed too close to his territory.

Legate Dominique plays the superficial Poseur in public while secretly and coldly preparing Paris's total annexation of the Fief on the Prince's behalf. @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} Keeper of Elysium Armand lives aboard his yacht, the White Rose, and holds court at the Atrium, a Rouen nightclub called Le Passage; Tremere Regent Alix de Chantraine uses the Fief's chaos as her own opportunity to rise within the English branch of her Clan.

Secret: Normandy's Kindred remain unaware that their Fief hosts one of the sinister Pentex corporation's principal French bases, especially active around Le Havre and Cherbourg's nuclear waste reprocessing facilities — drawing Garou war parties who consider the Fief's vampires complicit servants of the Wyrm. Only the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel} Osmont has noticed and warned Antifer, who has kept the warning to himself, hoping to seize power once the Garou finish off the Kindred of the surface.

This Fief unites two older domains: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue}-ruled Aquitaine (centered on Bordeaux) and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} Occitania (centered on the "Pink City" of Toulouse, historic seat of France's oldest @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} lineage, now nearly extinguished); Montpellier forms a third, more cosmopolitan city. @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} Marquis Edouard de Morsac, the last of the old Anglo-Aquitaine Ventrue lineage and architect of Bordeaux's economic prosperity, rules from Bordeaux behind a courteous, reserved public manner that conceals a proud and merciless political operator; many suspect him of having orchestrated the disappearance of the Occitan Toreador line in 1793.

@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} Primogen representative Ferdinand, who once led the Anarchs who briefly seized Toulouse during the Terror, is accused by his own Idealist rivals of using that chaos to eliminate his internal @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} opponents; he seeks to reclaim Occitania as an independent Brujah territory. Unbeknownst to Ferdinand, he has long been a puppet of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} Nathanael, an unnervingly persuasive manipulator (rumored to hold the Discipline of Dementation) who is secretly a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} agent tasked with destabilizing the local @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}.

Secret: the Toreador Prince of Occitania, Amaury, believed annihilated along with his entire retinue on the night of 13 September 1793 in a massacre blamed variously on the Ventrue, the Brujah, and the Parisian Toreador, in fact survived. Nathanael dragged him from the slaughter, drove him mad with Dementation, and had his face altered by a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} ally to prevent recognition. Amaury now wanders as the pitiful, amnesiac @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} Soliman, haunting regional hospitals and asylums, thrown into abject terror by the mere mention of Nathanael's name. Should Soliman ever recover his memory and prove his identity, the ancient Pact of the Two Roses would obligate Prince Villon to recognize his claim to the Fief — a revelation that could shatter the Parisian Hegemony itself.

The lone surviving Occitan Toreador, Legate Aymeric (who escaped the 1793 massacre only because he was in Barcelona at the time), quietly builds his own power base at the Elysium and is rumored to intend eventually declaring himself Prince of a liberated Toulouse. The ancient @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} Antonio, sole known representative of his Clan in the Fief after the Terror wiped out the rest, wanders the sewers between cities, a keeper of centuries of secrets who never intervenes directly in local politics.

Founded by Greek colonists in the 7th century BC and ruled from the start by an alliance of @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador}, Marseille is France's oldest Kindred Fief and the country's most volatile. Nominal @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} Marquis Villeneuve, a 19th-century industrialist Ancilla, wields only symbolic authority; the Primogen has always managed Marseille's affairs independent of any central power, and the city is currently sliding toward outright civil war between five factions: the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}, the Anarchs, the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni}, the Setites, and the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}, which is more deeply entrenched here than in any other French Fief.

The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} Idealist Gorias, Embraced in the late 14th century by the legendary Marius (who dreamed of a Brujah "new Carthage" at Marseille), is the oldest known vampire in the city and the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}'s chief local opponent; he seeks to restore the old Brujah-led "Free Republic" that governed Marseille from 1757 until the Revolution. Valeria, an Italian communist militant Embraced in 1937 during the Spanish Civil War, now coordinates the city's Anarch cells with Gorias's protection; Villeneuve is rumored to have contracted the Assamites to eliminate her.

The reclusive @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} Memmon, called "king" by his own Clan and rumored to be a Methuselah, may be the city's true secret power, playing every faction — the Sabbat, the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni}, the Setites — against the others to keep Marseille locked in permanent, useful chaos. Legate and Keeper of Elysium Gabrielle is loathed by the local @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} as a traitor for currying the Marquis's favor at their expense; her chief rival, Maxime (descended from the legendary Geneviève Orseau), leads the anti-Hegemony Toreador faction and has begun weighing an unthinkable alliance with Gorias's Brujah against Paris. @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} lieutenant Roche, a former Marseille gangster Embraced by Villeneuve in the 1930s, still carries himself like the mobster he was, his old underworld influence steadily eroded by the rising Giovanni. The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} "queen" Tanis runs a vast smuggling network in stolen art, earning her both the favor and the enmity of Toreador across France, Italy, and Spain.

Secret: Xarca, the ancient @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} Queen of Marseille believed destroyed in the 15th-century Sabbat schism, in fact survived by feigning her own destruction and slipping into torpor in a hidden crypt for nearly five centuries. Recently awakened and still half-dormant, she now secretly directs several of the city's Kindred — her chief pawns, with bitter irony, being the very Sabbat @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} who believe themselves independent of any Elder's control.

Lyon, France's third city and once one of its great economic centers, has a long tradition of independence from Paris dating to its founding as Roman Lugdunum. @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} Marquis De Vandreuil, Embraced in the early 16th century, rules with an iron hand in appearance only: his true power has steadily bled away to the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni}, whose financial backing rebuilt the Fief after the Revolution and who now effectively control its economy while De Vandreuil serves as their political front. Fiercely resentful of the Hegemony, De Vandreuil helped found the Praxist movement and is a leading advocate of restoring full Princely sovereignty to every Marquis; few of his allies know that he had his own sire eliminated and struck a private bargain with the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni} to secure his throne. His descendant Catherine de Vandreuil, an elegant and efficient "executive woman" recently Embraced from her long service as his devoted ghoul, now manages the Marquis's public relations with Lyon's mortal elite.

@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} Keeper of Elysium Côme, a genuine Renaissance-trained painter, sculptor, and poet from Florence rather than a mere Poseur, reserves his art for his Clan's elite and is rumored to have refused to open his private gallery even to the Prince of Paris; the Fief's Atrium is a nocturnal art gallery run by his loyal servant Antonelli. @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} Regent Morens, unusually principled for his Clan, has launched his Chantry into open opposition against Giovanni influence in the Fief, an unusual role as unlikely defender of @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} authority. The Giovanni representative Adriana, coldly beautiful and razor-witted, works to complete her Clan's takeover of the city, already dominant in Nice and heavily entrenched in Marseille.

Secret: Lyon is Inconnu's principal base in France. Beneath the city, an ancient network of tunnels shelters a cabal of Inconnu @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu}, Malkavians, and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} led by Magnus, Lugdunum's first Ventrue Prince, who in truth faked his own destruction in a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra}-set fire in the year 65 and has secretly observed and manipulated the city's Kindred politics for nearly two thousand years. The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} Silence, De Vandreuil's Provost, is in fact one of Magnus's agents, having stoked the Marquis's persecution of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} and now preparing to inflame the secret war between the Giovanni and the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} — both Clans the Inconnu regard as uniquely dangerous to their absolute secrecy.

Centered on Strasbourg (seat of the European Parliament), Metz, and Nancy, the Fief de l'Est has spent centuries torn between French and German influence. @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} Marquise Anna Schelling, Embraced at the close of the last century by a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} finance baron, champions reconciliation between French and German Kindred and a unified European Ventrue confederation, a vision that has begun to bear fruit since Strasbourg became seat of the European Council in 1949; behind the visionary image lies a shrewd, self-interested businesswoman working to loosen the Fief from Parisian control. Her chief internal rival, the Prussian Elder Friedrich von Köln (Embraced in the 16th century by Prince Gustav of Berlin), leads the reactionary Ventrue "old guard" and patiently awaits Schelling's fall.

@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} Anarch leader and "Baron of Thionville" Frantz V, Embraced in 1930s Berlin, fought alongside the Spartacists against the Nazis before fleeing to France and the Resistance; he has since organized the Fief's Anarchs (based in the Ventrue-abandoned steel town of Thionville) into one of France's most coherent and effective Anarch movements. The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} Primogen representative Rosenkrantz, an alchemist-physician from the 14th century, pursues an unknown agenda in near-total isolation from Fief politics.

@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} Keeper of Elysium Justine Weiss, a Strasbourg-born dancer Embraced in 1863 who returned home after 1918 to found the Opéra du Rhin, has actively supported Schelling's reconciliation policy since the 1920s; the Atrium is a nightclub called the Danse Macabre. @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} Regent Wiener, an ambitious diplomat between the French and German Chantries, openly aims to succeed the current (reportedly insane) @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} Lord of France.

Secret: in the 15th century, a mysterious lineage of vampires called the Kyasid, led by their founder Marconius, seized Strasbourg for nearly a century before vanishing as abruptly as they arrived. Only Rosenkrantz has ever learned the truth: the half-vampire, half-fae Kyasid sought a hidden Regio — a fragment of the Dreaming accessible through a Gate hidden in a crypt beneath Strasbourg Cathedral — where they built a decaying, Bosch-like pocket city populated by the enslaved descendants of kidnapped mortals, sealed off from ordinary vampires and mortals alike. Rosenkrantz has made several undetected incursions into the Kyasid domain over the past century; the Tremere have noticed his unusual interest in the Cathedral and begun quietly investigating.

pages.name: Minor Domains: Brittany, Provence, Nice, Corsica, and Beyond

text.content:
Beyond the capital and the six major Fiefs, several smaller territories carry particular Kindred significance. The Fief du Vannetais (Nantes/Saint-Nazaire), theoretically still an independent @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} domain, has suffered a spectacular economic decline engineered by rival Bordeaux @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue}; its current Marquis, driven nearly to madness by the defeat, rules over what is now practically a deserted Fief. Brittany remains a land of deep-rooted fae tradition, sheltering many Mages, Changelings, and even a few Garou; the rare vampires who linger there have learned to avoid confrontation with the region's other supernatural residents entirely.

Provence is considered the personal Fief of Geneviève Orseau, the oldest known French @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador}, credited with having driven Setite influence out of southern France centuries ago; Avignon, famous for its arts festival, remains a favored retreat for @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} of every lineage. Nice, only recently annexed to France and still regarded by French Kindred as foreign territory, is almost entirely controlled by Clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni}, particularly through the region's casino industry. The Centre of France is not truly a Fief in its own right, but its principal towns (Blois, Tours, and others) shelter the political and financial interests of powerful Parisian Toreador and Ventrue.

Corsica has for centuries been the scene of bloody clashes between rival @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} factions, some tied to the Sicilian Mafia, now increasingly expressed through Corsican autonomist politics. The Basque Country's only active French vampires are Anarch @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel} and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} allied with regional autonomist movements and Spanish Anarchs across the border — making it the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel} Clan's last significant French stronghold. The French Antilles have been almost entirely abandoned by mainland Kindred amid persistent rumors of growing Setite influence in the region, save for a small colony of decadent Toreador who have severed all ties to their Clan.

vtmlarp.source: Le Monde des Ténèbres: France (France by Night), Chapter One: Les Vampires de France
